title: Brik Pipeline Report Fragment v1.1
description: Per-stage report fragment emitted by stage.run after each stage completes. v1.1 introduces a typed business outcome (status, reason) and the tech.kind label, while removing the legacy tech.warning / tech.warning_reason fields that conflated technical and business concerns. See chantier docs/chantiers/20260510_tech-business-orthogonal-axes.md for the full rationale.

stage.description: Stage name (lower-case, kebab-case for multi-word names).

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone offset, recorded when the fragment is written (after the stage logic returns).

duration_ms.description: Stage wall-clock duration in milliseconds. Optional. Mirrors the value already recorded by summary.build.

rc.description: Stage exit code as returned by the stage logic. 0 = success or skipped, non-zero = failure. Code 99 (SKIP_WITH_WARNING) is removed in v1.1.

status.description: Technical stage status, derived from rc. 'skipped' covers auto-detected not-applicable cases. v1.1 no longer uses 'skipped' for user-disabled stages: that decision moves to the business layer.

platform.description: CI platform on which this stage ran.

image.description: Docker image reference of the runner container, when applicable.

job_url.description: Direct URL to the CI job log, when the platform exposes one.

tech.description: Technical traceability payload. v1.1 explicitly rejects the legacy tech.warning / tech.warning_reason fields (those decisions are now expressed via business.status), but keeps the block open (additionalProperties: true) so per-stage runtime telemetry (build_duration_ms, framework, image_built, ...) can land without bumping the schema. The known fields below describe the shape consumers can rely on.

status.description: Mirror of the top-level status. Kept for producer convenience.

kind.description: Human-readable label derived from rc, used in reports and recap. Maps to the BRIK_EXIT_* table.

exit_code.description: Stage exit code as captured by the runtime. Mirror of top-level rc, kept for compatibility with v1.0 producers.

duration_ms.description: Stage wall-clock duration in milliseconds. Mirror of top-level duration_ms.

stack.description: Stack identifier (node, python, java, rust, dotnet, docker, ...).

tool.description: Tool resolved by the stage logic (e.g. 'eslint', 'semgrep', 'jest').

command.description: Command line invoked by the stage, with arguments. '<stack-default>' when the stage selected its default command.

business.description: Business outcome payload. v1.1 makes status mandatory and typed (success / warning / error) so the runtime expresses outcomes the same way every consumer (notify, recap, harness E2E) reads them. Stage-specific business signals live under the known sub-blocks below; the block stays open (additionalProperties: true) so stages can also write top-level scalars (release.{bump_type, new_version, previous_version}, init.{platform, project_name, triggered_by}, ...) without bumping the schema.

status.description: Business outcome. Derived by lib/pipeline/business.sh from (tech, side-band signals, pipeline.context).

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Required by convention when status != success, but the schema does not enforce it (consumers fall back to tech.kind when absent).

findings.description: Open sub-block carrying findings counts and metadata for security / quality stages. The block stays open (additionalProperties: true) so FMF L4 fields (total, by_severity, ignored.*) continue to land without a schema bump. The 'failing' sub-block is typed strict: it carries the fix-exists classification counters introduced in v1.1 by the master pipeline-behavior-model chantier.

failing.description: Fix-exists classification counters for the failing subset. Optional: a stage that produces no failing findings is not required to write this block. When present, total / has_fix / no_fix are non-negative integers. has_fix counts findings with an upstream fix available; no_fix counts findings without one (no-upstream-fix, vendor-wont-fix); total counts all failing findings (equals has_fix + no_fix + unknown-classification entries).

tests.description: Open sub-block carrying test counts and coverage data for the test stage.

artifact.description: Open sub-block describing the build artifact produced by the build stage.

image.description: Open sub-block describing the container image produced by the package stage.

registry.description: Open sub-block describing the registry coordinates of a published artifact.
